parsed.explanation: Traveler-facing exposures are minimal: no criminalisation of gender expression, freedom from GI-based arbitrary arrest affirmed 2011–2024, X-marker passports accepted, self-ID climate, working anti-discrimination law with a court award for a trans woman, and one of the world's most welcoming destinations. The negatives are modest and mostly not visitor-facing: the 2024 supreme court custody-placement ruling applies to inmates (a detained visitor could face birth-sex placement, an open question rather than documented visitor practice); hate-crime law omits gender identity; one 2024 murder of a trans migrant (single incident, weak rate evidence); recurring hate speech and some reported service denial. No universal facility bans, no police targeting, no organised campaigns. Documented acceptance plus functioning institutions place this in Low Risk, near the 0.85 anchor, held back by custody uncertainty and narrow hate-crime recourse rather than any unremedied traveler exposure.
